purpose: Adalimumab-atto is used to treat several conditions where the immune system attacks the body, including rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, and plaque psoriasis. It helps reduce pain, swelling, and inflammation. It can also slow down joint damage in certain types of arthritis.
how_it_works: Your immune system makes a protein called TNF (tumor necrosis factor) that can cause inflammation. When too much TNF is made, it can damage your joints, skin, and intestines. This medication works by blocking TNF, which helps calm down the overactive immune response and reduce inflammation.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include redness, pain, or swelling at the injection site, headache, and rash. You may also experience cold-like symptoms such as runny nose or sore throat. Some people notice stomach pain or nausea as well.
warnings: Because this medication lowers your immune system's activity, you are more likely to get serious infections, including tuberculosis (TB). Your doctor will test you for TB before you start. Avoid this medication if you have an active infection. It may also increase the risk of certain cancers. Tell your doctor right away if you develop fever, chills, or signs of infection. Do not receive live vaccines while on this medication.
typical_dosing: This medication is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous injection). The dose and how often you take it depends on the condition being treated. For example, for rheumatoid arthritis, it is typically one injection (40 mg) every other week. Your doctor will tell you the right dose and schedule for your specific condition. It comes as a pre-filled pen or syringe for home use.
